metadata.note: The Northern Pacific Railway's main line across the Idaho panhandle, via Clark Fork and Sandpoint on Lake Pend Oreille, connecting Montana to Spokane, WA -- the NP's own transcontinental route, completed 1883 (last-spike ceremony at Gold Creek, MT, Sept 8 1883), a year ahead of the Union Pacific's Oregon Short Line across southern Idaho (see union_pacific_oregon_short_line-style file osl.geojson). Geometry traced through real track using OpenStreetMap data (Overpass API) and shortest-path graph search; the corridor remains BNSF's busy 'Kootenai River Subdivision' today. Note that the historic Great Northern main line (see great_northern.geojson) also crossed the panhandle nearby, and after the 1970 Burlington Northern merger, through traffic in this specific stretch consolidated onto what was substantially the ex-NP alignment -- Amtrak's Empire Builder still stops at Sandpoint's original 1916 NP depot today, so this line's real successor service is already shown in great_northern.geojson/amtrak.geojson rather than duplicated here; this feature's own segments stop at the North Coast Limited's 1971 discontinuance.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Northern Pacific Railway, North Coast Limited), trains.com (Sandpoint, Idaho hotspot), spokanehistorical.org (Sandpoint Train Depot), unisco.com (Sandpoint rail yard)
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
